generated: read out of Art/dialogueBubbleRig.js at its defaults — regenerate, never hand-edit

grid.why: The bubble is an object IN the scene (diegetic doctrine), so it is authored on the same grid as the props it stands among — 32 px/m, the assets grid every shipped rig in this repo bakes at. The 24 px/m grid is the camera-side number (memory two-pixel-grids-ppu-vs-assetsppu); authoring there would put UI pixels on a different pitch from world pixels and the bubble would read as an overlay.
grid.crop: Every piece is an integer px count at this grid, so a 24-grid import is a straight rescale decision for the wiring PR, not a re-author.

light.built: inner light row directly under the top edge, shade row directly above the bottom edge
light.keyline: none beyond the panel ink ring (ADR 0031) — the ring is the object edge, not an outline pass
light.states: ONE lit state; the day/night grade is the in-engine layer (bible §6)

type.face: newly drawn for this kit, 2026-08-17 — nothing borrowed, no licence to carry
type.lowercase: YES — full a–z with a 4-row x-height, ascenders to cap height, and 2 descender rows (g j p q y)
type.caseRuling: speech body in sentence case (owner, 2026-08-17: both references set speech mixed, and that is why their dialogue reads as voice not signage). Name chip and option rows stay CAPS — labels, not voice.

costSplit.drawingTheLowercaseSet: DONE in this pass — 26 lowercase glyphs + repositioned points. No layout cost of its own.
costSplit.tallerLineBox: cell 4×8 → 5×10: +1 px advance, +2 px line height. A 22-col 4-line panel goes 97×39 → 119×48 (+23% w, +23% h); the option ladder goes 30/41/52 → 34/47/60 px (+13 per row).
costSplit.whyBoth: Reported separately because only the second one moves any other number. It was taken ONCE, before the freeze, so every derived value below is already the mixed-case value.

type.fill: one cell per character, left to right, line by line; layout.rows[] gives each line its cell origin, and layout.chars the total the cadence divides

optionFormula.step: +13 px per row (34 / 47 / 60 px for 2 / 3 / 4 rows)

case.labels: name chip and option rows in CAPS

panel.textBox: x+5, y+5, w-10, h-10 — the rect text may fill, measured, not derived

slices.note: corners copied, edges repeated 1 px, centre flat paper

panel.ladderNote: type.ladder is the full cols × lines table with panel px, text box and chars per line

tail.anchorRule: the tip pixel is THE anchor — the presenter aims it at the speaker anchor. tail.tip is given relative to the tail sprite origin; layoutSay() returns it in bubble space.
tail.upSet: SHIPPED, not flipped at import: leftUp / centreUp / rightUp anchor a bubble BELOW the speaker, for a speaker near the top of the screen. A tail is 2 colours with NO shading, so a y-flip fights nothing in the panel light — but the kit performs it so the import never has to reason about it, and so the tip pixel is measured in both directions.
tail.join: the tail's edge row overwrites the panel's edge row on that side, so the ink ring opens and the paper is continuous
tail.gapNote: px the tip stops CLEAR OF THE SPRITE INK, not of the anchor: mount({clear}) takes the anchor→ink-edge distance (the head anchor is the head centre, so 3 px off the anchor would bury the tip in the crown). The harness measures clear off the rig’s own alpha — 7 px for the adult idle at dir 4.
tail.chipInteraction: the chip rides the edge AWAY from the tail — top-left for down tails, bottom-left for up tails — so a name and a tail never fight for a corner

chip.mount: x + 4, y − (h − 4) for down tails; y + panelH − 4 for up tails
chip.perSpeakerTint: FLAGGED, not built — a tint would slot at chip.paper only; the ink and the ramp steps stay.

options.ladder: +13 px per row (34 / 47 / 60 px for 2 / 3 / 4 rows)
options.gutterNote: the 11 px gutter is the cursor lane — the cursor never overlaps text

highlight.label: GOLD PILL
highlight.note: Cove gold behind the row, dark ink on it. The AC read in fleet colours; the one place a saturated colour is allowed, because selection is the one thing that must never be missed.

highlight.label: INVERTED ROW
highlight.note: Ink and paper swap. No new colour at all, and it survives any grade — but it reads as a redaction on paper stock.

highlight.label: GOLD RULE
highlight.note: Paper stays, a gold rule under the row. Lightest touch, leans hardest on the cursor to carry the state.

highlight.label: PRESSED ROW
highlight.note: The row is inset a pixel with its own shade above and light below, so selection is a physical state of the object. Quietest, and the only one that costs no colour.

options.invariant: THE RULE: neither bubble ever occludes the speaker's sprite rect (the character IS the portrait). speakerClear = 20 px is ONE implementation of it; screenBudget() is the proof at a zoom tier.
options.mount: optionsMount(sayLayout, {bounds}): hangs off the speech bubble on the side AWAY from the tail (below it for down tails, above it for up tails), keeping speakerClear from the tail column
options.mountFallback: the away side is a preference, not a guarantee — a below-right tail near the left edge of the screen has no room there. Pass bounds {x0,x1} (drawable span, same coordinate space) and the mount takes the side that fits, returning side / away / clearFromTail / clamped. clamped:true means neither side fits: shorten the rows or move the camera, do not nudge pixels.

cursor.label: POINTING HAND
cursor.note: Redrawn 2026-08-17 (pass 1 read as a hand/pointer hybrid): a closed fist with a thumb knuckle, and an index finger that leaves it as a THREE-row form — ink line, lit paper row, ink line — so the finger is a cylinder against the fist mass instead of a spur off a blob. Owner’s pick.

cursor.label: WOOL WORK GLOVE
cursor.note: The same hand with a knitted cuff instead of a wrist. The owner’s "most ours" — worth a live trial; it costs one row and a dark band the row highlight also wants.

cursor.label: BRASS TACK
cursor.note: An object pressed into the row instead of a hand — no anatomy to get wrong at this size. Reads as a rivet before it reads as a pointer.

cursor.label: FISH HOOK
cursor.note: Charming at 6x, ambiguous at 1x (owner, 2026-08-17 — check the 1x row on the board before keeping it). It also points with its barb, which is a threat, not an invitation.

marker.shape: 7x4 solid triangle, ink ring + paper fill
marker.anim: 2-frame idle bob, +1 px, 420 ms per frame
marker.mount: x + w − 11, y + h − 2 — rides the bottom edge, right of centre, clear of every tail

caret.shape: 1 × 6 ink bar in the cell the next character lands in
caret.shown: while filling only; it hands off to the continue marker when the line completes
caret.why: the sound IS the bubble populating — the caret is the visible half of that cadence

stocks.label: WARM CREAM PAPER
stocks.provenance: paper/hi/lo = KTC_HOUS steps 4/5/3 (lobsterBoatVariantsIsoRig.js) · edge = KTC_BOOT[2] · ink = HAIRS.black[2] (headIsoRig3.js)
stocks.note: The Animal Crossing read in harbour colours — the fleet house cream, so the bubble is painted from the same tin as the boats it stands in front of.

stocks.label: GREY NEWSPRINT
stocks.provenance: calendarRig.js DAY.paper / paperHi / paperLo / ink / inkSoft
stocks.note: The wall calendar's cheap stock. Right if speech should read as printed matter; wrong if the bubble should feel warmer than the town's paperwork.

stocks.label: SAILCLOTH
stocks.provenance: paper = ShoreFinds BONE · hi = KTC_HOUS[5] · lo/inkSoft = HATCOLS.oat[3]/[1] · ink/edge = ShoreFinds KEYLINE
stocks.note: Bone-white canvas, cooler and flatter than cream. Reads as harbour kit rather than as paper — the owner’s pick as the strongest alternate if cream ever feels too AC.

stocks.label: ENAMEL BOARD
stocks.provenance: paper/hi/lo = KTC_HOUS steps 3/4/1 · ink/edge = KTC_BOOT[1]/[0] · inkSoft = BOOT[3] (headIsoRig3.js)
stocks.note: Pale enamel over a hard dark edge — the boats’ house sides. The most object-like, the least paper-like; the ink ring goes near-black.

occupancy.rule: the speech panel, the name chip and the option bubble never occlude the speaker's sprite rect — the character IS the portrait. speakerClear (20 px) is one implementation of it, not the rule.
occupancy.tailRule: the TAIL is the pointer and the exception: it reaches towards the speaker and stops gap (3 px) clear of the sprite ink, measured through mount({clear}) rather than guessed from the anchor. clear is DIRECTIONAL — a down tail clears the crown, an up tail hangs the bubble below the FEET (below the head is her body), so aim an up tail at the hip/foot anchor or pass the anchor→ink-bottom distance.
occupancy.assumption: output 1920×1080, per-tier pixel-perfect zoom (ruling #327). If the shipped tier ladder differs, pass tiers[] — the arithmetic does not change.

api.layoutSay: layoutSay(x,y,o) — same maths, nothing drawn (top/bottom include chip and tail)
api.mount: mount(anchor,o) -> {x,y} so the tail tip lands on the speaker anchor, above or below by tail dir
api.pieces: panel · tail · chip · cursor · marker · caret · slices(w,h)
api.metrics: metricsTable({cols,lines,optCols}) — the line arithmetic the fill needs
api.sheet: sheet({stock}) -> canvas · sheetSpec({stock}) -> the same crop-box table as data

talkCues.appliesTo: characterIsoRig6.js (pass 6.3) and any pass that keeps its anchors() contract
talkCues.mechanism: draw-time integer screen offset + a marker. No new baked clip, no re-bake, no sheet.

facings.why: the cue is a screen-VERTICAL offset, the one axis that does not rotate with the ground bearing, so one cue is correct at all eight rows with nothing authored per row
facings.marker: anchored to CharacterIso.anchors(dir).head, which the body rig already resolves per facing

body.lift: 1 px — at 32 px/m a 2 px talk bounce reads as a nod, not as speech
body.settle: 210 ms: one last lift, then still — the line ending has to be visible without the text
body.integer: whole pixels only; the sprite is blitted, never scaled

mouth.state: ALREADY SHIPPING — no rig edit needed
mouth.call: CharacterIso6.render(dir, {t, talk:true, expr}) — pose() forwards opts to HeadIso.look() as its `rock` argument
mouth.drive: talk = (fill < 1). The mouth stops the instant the bubble finishes populating.
mouth.probe: TalkCue.probeMouth(CharacterIso6) — renders the same frame twice at one t, talk on and off, and asserts the diff is mouth-sized and sits in the lower face. The claim is a test; run it in the import PR and fail on it.

emotes.label: SURPRISE
emotes.note: The hop is the read; the marker only confirms it.

emotes.label: LAUGH
emotes.note: Four bobs on the beat — the only cue that repeats.

emotes.label: THINK
emotes.note: Stillness IS the cue. The body stops bouncing and the dots do the work.

exprMap.think: worry (closest of the eight in headIsoRig3.EXPRS; a real "pondering" expression would be a head-rig ask, not a cue-layer one)

markerMount.place: 'above' with no bubble up, 'side' (beside the head, centred on the anchor) while a speech bubble owns the space above
markerMount.side: pass the side away from the bubble tail
markerMount.pop: 2 frames — inset 1 px for the first ~12% of the emote, then full

api.body: body({t, talking, startedAt, stoppedAt, emote, emoteAt}) -> {dy, beat, phase, state}
api.charOpts: charOpts(o) -> the opts object to spread into CharacterIso*.render
api.marker: marker(ctx, x, y, kind, {t, stock})  ·  markerAt(headAnchor, {emote, side}) -> box
api.probeMouth: probeMouth(CharacterIso6, {dir, samples, maxPx}) -> {pass, px, t, bbox, rowsBelowHeadAnchor}

openAsks: A one-line rig courtesy: characterIsoRig6 reaches the head talk channel through its `rock` argument. It works — probeMouth() proves it — but the name lies. Rename or alias it in the rig PR, KEEPING THE STABLE IDS: `rock` is the sixth positional argument of pose() and is read as arguments[5]; render() / pose() / anchors() signatures and the opts keys (t, talk, expr) must stay exactly as they are, or every consumer page and this kit break at once. Alias first, deprecate later.
Emphasis beats are uniform every 4th beat. Punctuation-driven emphasis (a beat held on a comma) wants the line parsed, which belongs to the dialogue system, not to art.
